# Swimlanes Diagram

**Source**: `mermaid-upstream/packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/swimlanes.md` (317 lines)
**Detector**: `src/diagrams/swimlanes/detector.ts` — `/^\s*swimlane-beta\b/`
**Minimum version**: v11.16.0
**Registry id**: `swimlanes`

> Upstream warns the syntax may evolve (`:8-10`). Keep the experimental marking.

**Note the keyword is singular**: `swimlane-beta`, while the diagram type is called
"Swimlanes". Getting this wrong is the first thing a user will do.

## Header And Direction (`:44-66`)

`swimlane-beta` with an optional direction: `TB`, `TD` (same as TB), `BT`, `LR`, `RL`.
**Defaults to `TB`** when omitted.

## Lanes (`:68-95`)

Lanes are `subgraph` blocks. **Top-level subgraphs render as swimlanes.**

```
subgraph Sales
  lead[Qualify lead]
end

subgraph sales [Sales team]
  lead[Qualify lead]
end
```

The id/label form is recommended for labels containing spaces and for stable styling targets.

## Nodes And Edges

Both reuse flowchart syntax (`:99`, `:137`). The page lists only the common forms and
defers to `flowchart.md` for the full catalog (`:133`, `:166`).

Common nodes: `id[Text]`, `id(Text)`, `id([Text])`, `id{Text}`, `id((Text))`.
Common edges: `A --> B`, `A --- B`, `A -->|Label| B`, `A -.-> B`, `A ==> B`.

Edge chaining works: `investigate --> fix --> answer` (`:40`).

`classDef` and `class` work as in flowchart (`:288-289`).

## Accessibility (`:168-190`)

`accTitle:` and `accDescr:`.

## Editor Notes

- **The dialect should be built on top of the flowchart dialect, not beside it.** Node
  shapes, edge operators, markdown strings, icons, images, classes and styling are all
  flowchart's, so this is flowchart's tokenizer plus lane semantics. Sharing the
  implementation is the point of having a `core/` layer in `packages/editor`.
- Everything in `../flowchart-shapes.md` applies here, including the 53 shapes and the
  `A@{ shape: … }` metadata form — the page says "see Flowchart syntax" rather than
  restating them.
- The flowchart gotchas carry over and deserve the same diagnostics: lowercase `end`
  breaking the parse, and a node label starting with `o` or `x` after a link.
- Fold `subgraph` … `end`.
- Completion for `direction` immediately after `swimlane-beta`.

Electricity grid,H2 conversion,27.14
```

### Quoting (`:129-149`)

- A value containing a comma must be double-quoted: `"Heating and cooling, homes"`.
- A literal double quote is escaped by doubling it, inside a quoted string:
  `"Heating and cooling, ""homes"""`.

These are standard CSV rules, but they are the two things people get wrong, and mermaid's
parse error will not explain them.

`%%` comments appear in the upstream example (`:109`) as a header row substitute.

## Configuration (`:151-251`)

| Option | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | number | — |
| `height` | number | — |
| `linkColor` | `source`, `target`, `gradient`, or a hex code | — |
| `nodeAlignment` | `justify`, `center`, `left`, `right` | — |
| `showValues` | boolean | — |
| `labelStyle` (v11.15.0+) | `legacy`, `outlined` | `legacy` |
| `nodeWidth` (v11.15.0+) | number, px | `10` |
| `nodePadding` (v11.15.0+) | number, px | `12` |
| `nodeColors` (v11.15.0+) | map of node name → CSS color | — |

`nodeColors` accepts hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` and named colors. Nodes not listed fall back to
the default scheme.

> `linkColor: 'gradient'` plus `nodeColors` is the hook for making sankey match the app
> palette. Wire it into `packages/ui/src/theme.ts`.

## Editor Notes

- **This dialect is a CSV parser, not a mermaid tokenizer.** Do not try to reuse the
  common statement layer beyond the header line.
- Highlighting: column 1 as source, column 2 as target, column 3 as number. Colouring the
  third column as a numeric literal makes a misaligned row visible instantly.
- Completion after a comma: node names already present in the document. This is the single
  most useful thing an editor can do for sankey, since node identity is by exact string
  and a typo silently creates a new node.
- Diagnostics, all of which mermaid reports badly or not at all:
  - a row with fewer or more than 3 columns;
  - a non-numeric third column;
  - an unterminated quoted field;
  - a node that appears only as a target and never as a source, or vice versa (a hint, not
    an error — it is often intentional at the graph edges);
  - **a typo'd node name**, detectable as a name used exactly once in the whole document.
- Because the format is CSV, paste-from-spreadsheet should work. Worth making the import
  path accept a pasted TSV and convert it.

1	# XY Chart
2	
3	> In the context of mermaid-js, the XY chart is a comprehensive charting module that encompasses various types of charts that utilize both x-axis and y-axis for data representation. Presently, it includes two fundamental chart types: the bar chart and the line chart. These charts are designed to visually display and analyze data that involve two numerical variables.
4	
5	> It's important to note that while the current implementation of mermaid-js includes these two chart types, the framework is designed to be dynamic and adaptable. Therefore, it has the capacity for expansion and the inclusion of additional chart types in the future. This means that users can expect an evolving suite of charting options within the XY chart module, catering to various data visualization needs as new chart types are introduced over time.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	```mermaid-example
10	xychart
11	    title "Sales Revenue"
12	    x-axis [jan, feb, mar, apr, may, jun, jul, aug, sep, oct, nov, dec]
13	    y-axis "Revenue (in $)" 4000 --> 11000
14	    bar [5000, 6000, 7500, 8200, 9500, 10500, 11000, 10200, 9200, 8500, 7000, 6000]
15	    line [5000, 6000, 7500, 8200, 9500, 10500, 11000, 10200, 9200, 8500, 7000, 6000]
16	```
17	
18	## Syntax
19	
20	```note
21	All text values that contain only one word can be written without `"`. If a text value has many words in it, specifically if it contains spaces, enclose the value in `"`
22	```
23	
24	### Orientations
25	
26	The chart can be drawn horizontal or vertical, default value is vertical.
27	
28	```
29	xychart horizontal
30	...
31	```
32	
33	### Title
34	
35	The title is a short description of the chart and it will always render on top of the chart.
36	
37	#### Example
38	
39	```
40	xychart
41	    title "This is a simple example"
42	    ...
43	```
44	
45	```note
46	If the title is a single word one no need to use `"`, but if it has space `"` is needed
47	```
48	
49	### x-axis
50	
51	The x-axis primarily serves as a categorical value, although it can also function as a numeric range value when needed.
52	
53	#### Example
54	
55	1. `x-axis title min --> max` x-axis will function as numeric with the given range
56	2. `x-axis "title with space" [cat1, "cat2 with space", cat3]` x-axis if categorical, categories are text type
57	
58	### y-axis
59	
60	The y-axis is employed to represent numerical range values, it cannot have categorical values.
61	
62	#### Example
63	
64	1. `y-axis title min --> max`
65	2. `y-axis title` it will only add the title, the range will be auto generated from data.
66	
67	```note
68	Both x and y axis are optional if not provided we will try to create the range
69	```
70	
71	### Line chart
72	
73	A line chart offers the capability to graphically depict lines.
74	
75	#### Example
76	
77	1. `line [2.3, 45, .98, -3.4]` it can have all valid numeric values.
78	2. `line "series name" [2.3, 45, .98, -3.4]` adds the line to the legend.
79	
80	### Bar chart
81	
82	A bar chart offers the capability to graphically depict bars.
83	
84	#### Example
85	
86	1. `bar [2.3, 45, .98, -3.4]` it can have all valid numeric values.
87	2. `bar "series name" [2.3, 45, .98, -3.4]` adds the bar to the legend.
88	
89	### Legend (v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)
90	
91	Named line and bar plots are automatically shown in a legend. Unnamed plots are omitted from the legend.
92	
93	```mermaid-example
94	xychart-beta
95	  title "An Example Chart"
96	  x-axis ["90d", "60d", "30d", "7d", "1d", "Current"]
97	  y-axis "Seconds" 0 --> 198.2
98	  line "avg" [48.1, 41.5, 45.7, 72.8, 67.7, 59.9]
99	  line "p50" [38.2, 36.8, 39.7, 54.5, 49.0, 38.4]
100	  line "p95" [112.2, 75.3, 103.0, 177.0, 180.2, 109.4]
101	```
102	
103	#### Simplest example
104	
105	The only two things required are the chart name (`xychart`) and one data set. So you will be able to draw a chart with a simple config like
106	
107	```
108	xychart
109	    line [+1.3, .6, 2.4, -.34]
110	```
111	
112	## Chart Configurations
113	
114	| Parameter                | Description                                                   | Default value |
115	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | :-----------: |
116	| width                    | Width of the chart                                            |      700      |
117	| height                   | Height of the chart                                           |      500      |
118	| titlePadding             | Top and Bottom padding of the title                           |      10       |
119	| titleFontSize            | Title font size                                               |      20       |
120	| showTitle                | Title to be shown or not                                      |     true      |
121	| showLegend               | Legend to be shown for named plots or not                     |     true      |
122	| legendFontSize           | Legend font size                                              |      14       |
123	| legendPadding            | Padding around the legend                                     |      10       |
124	| xAxis                    | xAxis configuration                                           |  AxisConfig   |
125	| yAxis                    | yAxis configuration                                           |  AxisConfig   |
126	| chartOrientation         | 'vertical' or 'horizontal'                                    |  'vertical'   |
127	| plotReservedSpacePercent | Minimum space plots will take inside the chart                |      50       |
128	| showDataLabel            | Should show the value corresponding to the bar within the bar |     false     |
129	| showDataLabelOutsideBar  | If showing data label then show it outside the bar.           |     false     |
130	
131	### AxisConfig
132	
133	| Parameter     | Description                                                  | Default value |
134	| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | :-----------: |
135	| showLabel     | Show axis labels or tick values                              |     true      |
136	| labelFontSize | Font size of the label to be drawn                           |      14       |
137	| labelPadding  | Top and Bottom padding of the label                          |       5       |
138	| showTitle     | Axis title to be shown or not                                |     true      |
139	| titleFontSize | Axis title font size                                         |      16       |
140	| titlePadding  | Top and Bottom padding of Axis title                         |       5       |
141	| showTick      | Tick to be shown or not                                      |     true      |
142	| tickLength    | How long the tick will be                                    |       5       |
143	| tickWidth     | How width the tick will be                                   |       2       |
144	| showAxisLine  | Axis line to be shown or not                                 |     true      |
145	| axisLineWidth | Thickness of the axis line                                   |       2       |
146	| labelRotation | Label rotation in degrees (only applicable on bottom X axis) |       0       |
147	
148	## Chart Theme Variables
149	
150	Themes for xychart reside inside the `xychart` attribute, allowing customization through the following syntax:
151	
152	```yaml
153	---
154	config:
155	  themeVariables:
156	    xyChart:
157	      titleColor: '#ff0000'
158	---
159	```
160	
161	| Parameter        | Description                                               |
162	| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
163	| backgroundColor  | Background color of the whole chart                       |
164	| titleColor       | Color of the Title text                                   |
165	| dataLabelColor   | Color of the Data labels (if shown)                       |
166	| legendTextColor  | Color of the legend text                                  |
167	| xAxisLabelColor  | Color of the x-axis labels                                |
168	| xAxisTitleColor  | Color of the x-axis title                                 |
169	| xAxisTickColor   | Color of the x-axis tick                                  |
170	| xAxisLineColor   | Color of the x-axis line                                  |
171	| yAxisLabelColor  | Color of the y-axis labels                                |
172	| yAxisTitleColor  | Color of the y-axis title                                 |
173	| yAxisTickColor   | Color of the y-axis tick                                  |
174	| yAxisLineColor   | Color of the y-axis line                                  |
175	| plotColorPalette | String of colors separated by comma e.g. "#f3456, #43445" |
176	
177	### Setting Colors for Lines and Bars
178	
179	To set the color for lines and bars, use the `plotColorPalette` parameter. Colors in the palette will correspond sequentially to the elements in your chart (e.g., first bar/line will use the first color specified in the palette).
180	
181	```mermaid-example
182	---
183	config:
184	  themeVariables:
185	    xyChart:
186	      plotColorPalette: '#000000, #0000FF, #00FF00, #FF0000'
187	---
188	xychart
189	title "Different Colors in xyChart"
190	x-axis "categoriesX" ["Category 1", "Category 2", "Category 3", "Category 4"]
191	y-axis "valuesY" 0 --> 50
192	%% Black line
193	line [10,20,30,40]
194	%% Blue bar
195	bar [20,30,25,35]
196	%% Green bar
197	bar [15,25,20,30]
198	%% Red line
199	line [5,15,25,35]
200	```
201	
202	## Displaying individual values on a bar chart (v11.14.0+)
203	
204	To show the value corresponding to a bar specify `showDataLabel: true`.
205	
206	```mermaid-example
207	---
208	config:
209	    xyChart:
210	        showDataLabel: true
211	---
212	xychart
213	    title "Genres in top 100 book survey of 2025"
214	    x-axis [comedy, romance, mystery, crime, "non fiction", other]
215	    y-axis "Number of Books" 0 --> 30
216	    bar [12,2,20,25,17,24]
217	```
218	
219	Labels are shown within the bar by default. To show the labels outside the bar, specify `showDataLabelOutsideBar: true`.
220	
221	```mermaid-example
222	---
223	config:
224	    xyChart:
225	        showDataLabel: true
226	        showDataLabelOutsideBar: true
227	---
228	xychart
229	    title "Genres in top 100 book survey of 2025"
230	    x-axis [comedy, romance, mystery, crime, "non fiction", other]
231	    y-axis "Number of Books" 0 --> 30
232	    bar [12,2,20,25,17,24]
233	```
234	
235	## Per-point text labels for line charts (v11.16.0+)
236	
237	Each data point in a `line` can optionally include a quoted string label after the numeric value. Labels render above points in vertical orientation, or to the right in horizontal orientation, using the line's stroke color.
238	
239	```mermaid-example
240	xychart
241	    title "Smallest AI models scoring above 60% on MMLU"
242	    x-axis "Date" ["Apr 2022", "Feb 2023", "Jul 2023", "Sep 2023", "Apr 2024"]
243	    y-axis "Parameters (B)" 0 --> 600
244	    line [540 "PaLM", 65 "LLaMA-65B", 34 "Llama 2 34B", 7 "Mistral 7B", 3.8 "Phi-3-mini"]
245	```
246	
247	Labels are optional per point — you can mix labeled and unlabeled values:
248	
249	```mermaid-example
250	xychart
251	    title "Quarterly Performance"
252	    x-axis [Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4]
253	    y-axis "Revenue ($M)" 0 --> 100
254	    line [25 "Launch", 45, 72, 90 "Target Hit"]
255	```
256	
257	Existing syntax without labels continues to work unchanged.
258	
259	```note
260	Point labels use a fixed font size of 12px. In vertical charts, labels appear above each point. In horizontal charts, labels appear to the right. Labels are currently supported on `line` plots only; the syntax is accepted on `bar` plots but labels are ignored.
261	```
262	
263	## Example on config and theme
264	
265	```mermaid-example
266	---
267	config:
268	    xyChart:
269	        width: 900
270	        height: 600
271	        showDataLabel: true
272	    themeVariables:
273	        xyChart:
274	            titleColor: "#ff0000"
275	---
276	xychart
277	    title "Sales Revenue"
278	    x-axis [jan, feb, mar, apr, may, jun, jul, aug, sep, oct, nov, dec]
279	    y-axis "Revenue (in $)" 4000 --> 11000
280	    bar [5000, 6000, 7500, 8200, 9500, 10500, 11000, 10200, 9200, 8500, 7000, 6000]
281	    line [5000, 6000, 7500, 8200, 9500, 10500, 11000, 10200, 9200, 8500, 7000, 6000]
282	```

1	# Architecture Diagrams Documentation (v11.1.0+)
2	
3	> In the context of mermaid-js, the architecture diagram is used to show the relationship between services and resources commonly found within the Cloud or CI/CD deployments. In an architecture diagram, services (nodes) are connected by edges. Related services can be placed within groups to better illustrate how they are organized.
4	
5	## Example
6	
7	```mermaid-example
8	architecture-beta
9	    group api(cloud)[API]
10	
11	    service db(database)[Database] in api
12	    service disk1(disk)[Storage] in api
13	    service disk2(disk)[Storage] in api
14	    service server(server)[Server] in api
15	
16	    db:L -- R:server
17	    disk1:T -- B:server
18	    disk2:T -- B:db
19	```
20	
21	## Syntax
22	
23	The building blocks of an architecture are `groups`, `services`, `edges`, and `junctions`.
24	
25	For supporting components, icons are declared by surrounding the icon name with `()`, while labels are declared by surrounding the text with `[]`.
26	
27	To begin an architecture diagram, use the keyword `architecture-beta`, followed by your groups, services, edges, and junctions. While each of the 3 building blocks can be declared in any order, care must be taken to ensure the identifier was previously declared by another component.
28	
29	### Groups
30	
31	The syntax for declaring a group is:
32	
33	```
34	group {group id}({icon name})[{title}] (in {parent id})?
35	```
36	
37	Put together:
38	
39	```
40	group public_api(cloud)[Public API]
41	```
42	
43	creates a group identified as `public_api`, uses the icon `cloud`, and has the label `Public API`.
44	
45	Additionally, groups can be placed within a group using the optional `in` keyword
46	
47	```
48	group private_api(cloud)[Private API] in public_api
49	```
50	
51	### Services
52	
53	The syntax for declaring a service is:
54	
55	```
56	service {service id}({icon name})[{title}] (in {parent id})?
57	```
58	
59	Put together:
60	
61	```
62	service database1(database)[My Database]
63	```
64	
65	creates the service identified as `database1`, using the icon `database`, with the label `My Database`.
66	
67	If the service belongs to a group, it can be placed inside it through the optional `in` keyword
68	
69	```
70	service database1(database)[My Database] in private_api
71	```
72	
73	### Edges
74	
75	The syntax for declaring an edge is:
76	
77	```
78	{serviceId}{{group}}?:{T|B|L|R} {<}?--{>}? {T|B|L|R}:{serviceId}{{group}}?
79	```
80	
81	#### Edge Direction
82	
83	The side of the service the edge comes out of is specified by adding a colon (`:`) to the side of the service connecting to the arrow and adding `L|R|T|B`
84	
85	For example:
86	
87	```
88	db:R -- L:server
89	```
90	
91	creates an edge between the services `db` and `server`, with the edge coming out of the right of `db` and the left of `server`.
92	
93	```
94	db:T -- L:server
95	```
96	
97	creates a 90 degree edge between the services `db` and `server`, with the edge coming out of the top of `db` and the left of `server`.
98	
99	#### Arrows
100	
101	Arrows can be added to each side of an edge by adding `<` before the direction on the left, and/or `>` after the direction on the right.
102	
103	For example:
104	
105	```
106	subnet:R --> L:gateway
107	```
108	
109	creates an edge with the arrow going into the `gateway` service
110	
111	#### Edges out of Groups
112	
113	To have an edge go from a group to another group or service within another group, the `{group}` modifier can be added after the `serviceId`.
114	
115	For example:
116	
117	```
118	service server[Server] in groupOne
119	service subnet[Subnet] in groupTwo
120	
121	server{group}:B --> T:subnet{group}
122	```
123	
124	creates an edge going out of `groupOne`, adjacent to `server`, and into `groupTwo`, adjacent to `subnet`.
125	
126	It's important to note that `groupId`s cannot be used for specifying edges and the `{group}` modifier can only be used for services within a group.
127	
128	### Aligning siblings (v11.16.0+)
129	
130	When several services share similar edge topology (for example, three databases all connecting `R --> L:mcp`), the layout heuristic may collapse them onto the same coordinate so that two render on top of each other. The `align` directive declares that a set of services share a row (same y) or a column (same x), and forces them to spread along that axis.
131	
132	```
133	align row {idA} {idB} {idC} ...
134	align column {idA} {idB} ...
135	```
136	
137	Members must already be declared as services or junctions, and at least two members are required. Each `align` directive lives on its own line.
138	
139	Pick the axis based on how the listed members are connected:
140	
141	- Use **`align column`** when the members connect to a common downstream node _via the same horizontal port pair_ (e.g. all use `R --> L:mcp`). They naturally form a vertical stack to one side, with parallel arrows reaching the downstream node.
142	- Use **`align row`** when the members connect to a common downstream node _via the same vertical port pair_ (e.g. all use `B --> T:proc`). They naturally form a horizontal row above the downstream node.
143	
144	Three databases all feeding `mcp` via right-to-left edges → stack them in a column:
145	
146	```mermaid-example
147	architecture-beta
148	    group api(cloud)[API]
149	    service db1(database)[DB1] in api
150	    service db2(database)[DB2] in api
151	    service db3(database)[DB3] in api
152	    service mcp(server)[MCP] in api
153	    db1:R --> L:mcp
154	    db2:R --> L:mcp
155	    db3:R --> L:mcp
156	    align column db1 db2 db3
157	```
158	
159	Three sources all feeding `proc` via top-to-bottom edges → arrange them in a row:
160	
161	```mermaid-example
162	architecture-beta
163	    service src1(server)[Source 1]
164	    service src2(server)[Source 2]
165	    service src3(server)[Source 3]
166	    service proc(server)[Processor]
167	    src1:B --> T:proc
168	    src2:B --> T:proc
169	    src3:B --> T:proc
170	    align row src1 src2 src3
171	```
172	
173	The order of members in the `align` directive determines their order along the axis. The gap between aligned members is controlled by `idealEdgeLengthMultiplier`.
174	
175	> **Note:** the declared order must not contradict the directions of edges between the listed members. For example, if the diagram contains `a:L --> R:b` (which places `a` to the right of `b`), then `align row a b` will conflict with that edge direction and the layout engine will fail to render. Use `align row b a` instead, or remove the conflicting edge.
176	
177	#### Grid layouts (combining `row` and `column`)
178	
179	`align row` only pins the y-coordinate of its members. To produce a clean grid where columns also align across tiers, pair each `align row` with one or more `align column` directives. The columns can span as many rows as you like — chain every node that should share an x-coordinate, even across groups.
180	
181	```mermaid-example
182	architecture-beta
183	    group sources(cloud)[Sources]
184	        service src_a(server)[Source A] in sources
185	        service src_b(server)[Source B] in sources
186	        service src_c(server)[Source C] in sources
187	
188	    group storage(database)[Storage]
189	        service db_one(database)[DB One] in storage
190	        service db_two(database)[DB Two] in storage
191	        service db_three(database)[DB Three] in storage
192	
193	    group output(disk)[Output]
194	        service brief(disk)[Brief] in output
195	        service analyst(server)[Analyst] in output
196	        service delivery(cloud)[Delivery] in output
197	
198	    src_a:B --> T:db_one
199	    src_b:B --> T:db_two
200	    src_c:B --> T:db_three
201	    db_two:B --> T:brief
202	    brief:R --> L:analyst
203	    analyst:R --> L:delivery
204	
205	    align row src_a src_b src_c
206	    align row db_one db_two db_three
207	    align row brief analyst delivery
208	
209	    align column src_a db_one
210	    align column src_b db_two brief
211	    align column src_c db_three
212	```
213	
214	The result is three left-to-right tiers stacked vertically with a straight spine through the middle column. Edges between aligned nodes render as straight horizontal or vertical lines; cross-axis edges (e.g. `db_one:R --> T:hub`) get a single 90° elbow.
215	
216	> **Tip:** if a long single-word label is too wide to fit on one line at small `iconSize` values, increase `iconSize` (or use a shorter title) to keep it on one line.
217	
218	### Junctions
219	
220	Junctions are a special type of node which acts as a potential 4-way split between edges.
221	
222	The syntax for declaring a junction is:
223	
224	```
225	junction {junction id} (in {parent id})?
226	```
227	
228	```mermaid-example
229	architecture-beta
230	    service left_disk(disk)[Disk]
231	    service top_disk(disk)[Disk]
232	    service bottom_disk(disk)[Disk]
233	    service top_gateway(internet)[Gateway]
234	    service bottom_gateway(internet)[Gateway]
235	    junction junctionCenter
236	    junction junctionRight
237	
238	    left_disk:R -- L:junctionCenter
239	    top_disk:B -- T:junctionCenter
240	    bottom_disk:T -- B:junctionCenter
241	    junctionCenter:R -- L:junctionRight
242	    top_gateway:B -- T:junctionRight
243	    bottom_gateway:T -- B:junctionRight
244	```
245	
246	## Configuration
247	
248	### `randomize` (v11.14.0+)
249	
250	By default, architecture diagrams start nodes at deterministic seed positions (`randomize: false`). Setting `randomize` to `true` randomizes initial node positions before running the layout algorithm, which may produce varied but potentially better-spaced layouts on each render.
251	
252	> Note: `randomize: false` alone is not enough to guarantee identical renders — the underlying fcose layout still calls `Math.random()` during its constraint solver. Use the `seed` option (described below) to lock the layout fully.
253	
254	Via frontmatter:
255	
256	```
257	---
258	config:
259	  architecture:
260	    randomize: true
261	---
262	architecture-beta
263	    group api(cloud)[API]
264	    service db(database)[Database] in api
265	    service server(server)[Server] in api
266	    db:R --> L:server
267	```
268	
269	Via `mermaid.initialize()`:
270	
271	```javascript
272	mermaid.initialize({
273	  architecture: {
274	    randomize: true,
275	  },
276	});
277	```
278	
279	| Option      | Type    | Default | Description                                                            |
280	| ----------- | ------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
281	| `randomize` | boolean | `false` | Whether to randomize initial node positions before running the layout. |
282	
283	### Layout tuning (v11.15.0+)
284	
285	The following options pass through to the underlying [fcose](https://github.com/iVis-at-Bilkent/cytoscape.js-fcose) layout so you can adjust spacing and density without changing your diagram source:
286	
287	| Option                      | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
288	| --------------------------- | ------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
289	| `nodeSeparation`            | number | `75`    | Minimum separation, in pixels, between sibling nodes in the same group. Pass-through to fcose.                                                                                                                                                   |
290	| `idealEdgeLengthMultiplier` | number | `1.5`   | Multiplier applied to `iconSize` to compute the ideal length of edges between nodes within the same group. Increase for breathing room, decrease to pack tighter. Cross-group edges are not affected.                                            |
291	| `edgeElasticity`            | number | `0.45`  | Spring elasticity (0–1) on same-group edges. Higher pulls connected nodes closer; lower lets them spread out. Cross-group edges are not affected.                                                                                                |
292	| `numIter`                   | number | `2500`  | Maximum fcose iterations. Increase for higher-quality layouts on large diagrams at the cost of render time.                                                                                                                                      |
293	| `seed`                      | number | `1`     | Deterministic seed for fcose. Defaults to `1` so the same diagram always renders with the same layout. Set to `0` to opt out and use native (non-deterministic) `Math.random`. Any other number selects a different reproducible layout variant. |
294	
295	Example — bumping `idealEdgeLengthMultiplier` stretches the spacing between connected nodes in a chain:
296	
297	```
298	---
299	config:
300	  architecture:
301	    idealEdgeLengthMultiplier: 3
302	---
303	architecture-beta
304	    service a(server)[A]
305	    service b(server)[B]
306	    service c(server)[C]
307	    a:R --> L:b
308	    b:R --> L:c
309	```
310	
311	> **Note:** these knobs tune fcose's force-directed layout; they do not change which nodes the layout heuristic considers adjacent. If two siblings render on top of each other because they share the same logical position in the spatial map (a known limitation tracked in [#6120](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/6120)), no combination of these knobs will move them apart — see the upcoming `align row|column` directive instead.
312	
313	## Icons
314	
315	By default, architecture diagram supports the following icons: `cloud`, `database`, `disk`, `internet`, `server`.
316	Users can use any of the 200,000+ icons available in iconify.design, or add other custom icons, by [registering an icon pack](../config/icons.md).
317	
318	After the icons are installed, they can be used in the architecture diagram by using the format "name:icon-name", where name is the value used when registering the icon pack.
319	
320	```mermaid-example
321	architecture-beta
322	    group api(logos:aws-lambda)[API]
323	
324	    service db(logos:aws-aurora)[Database] in api
325	    service disk1(logos:aws-glacier)[Storage] in api
326	    service disk2(logos:aws-s3)[Storage] in api
327	    service server(logos:aws-ec2)[Server] in api
328	
329	    db:L -- R:server
330	    disk1:T -- B:server
331	    disk2:T -- B:db
332	```
333

# XY Chart

**Source**: `mermaid-upstream/packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/xyChart.md` (282 lines)
**Detector**: `src/diagrams/xychart/xychartDetector.ts` — `/^\s*xychart(-beta)?/`
**Registry id**: `xychart`

Currently bar and line only; upstream says the module is designed to grow (`:5`).

## Quoting Rule (`:20-22`)

**Single-word values need no quotes; anything containing a space must be quoted.** This
applies to titles, axis titles and categories, and it is the most common source of
confusing parse errors in this type.

## Statements

| Keyword | Form |
| --- | --- |
| header | `xychart` or `xychart horizontal` (default vertical) |
| `title` | `title "Sales Revenue"` |
| `x-axis` | `x-axis title min --> max` (numeric) or `x-axis "title" [cat1, "cat 2"]` (categorical) |
| `y-axis` | `y-axis title min --> max`, or `y-axis title` for auto range |
| `line` | `line [2.3, 45, .98, -3.4]`, `line "series name" [...]` |
| `bar` | `bar [2.3, 45, .98, -3.4]`, `bar "series name" [...]` |

- The x-axis is categorical by default but can be a numeric range.
- **The y-axis cannot be categorical** (`:60`).
- Both axes are optional; ranges are derived from the data when absent (`:67-69`).
- Minimum valid diagram: `xychart` plus one data set (`:103-110`).
- Negative values and leading-dot decimals (`.98`) are valid.

## Legend

Version gate is the unresolved placeholder `v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+` (`:89`).
**Named plots appear in the legend; unnamed plots are omitted.** So `line "avg" [...]`
is the difference between a legend entry and none.

## Per-Point Labels (v11.16.0+) (`:235-261`)

A quoted string may follow each numeric value in a `line`:

```
line [540 "PaLM", 65 "LLaMA-65B", 3.8 "Phi-3-mini"]
line [25 "Launch", 45, 72, 90 "Target Hit"]     mixing is allowed
```

Fixed 12px font. Above points when vertical, to the right when horizontal.

> **Accepted on `bar` but silently ignored** (`:260`). A silent no-op deserves a
> diagnostic — the user has no way to tell it did not work.

## Data Labels (v11.14.0+) (`:202-233`)

`showDataLabel: true` shows the value inside the bar; add `showDataLabelOutsideBar: true`
to move it outside.

## Configuration (`:112-146`)

`width` (700), `height` (500), `titlePadding` (10), `titleFontSize` (20), `showTitle`
(true), `showLegend` (true), `legendFontSize` (14), `legendPadding` (10), `xAxis`/`yAxis`
(AxisConfig), `chartOrientation` (`'vertical'`), `plotReservedSpacePercent` (50),
`showDataLabel` (false), `showDataLabelOutsideBar` (false).

**AxisConfig**: `showLabel` (true), `labelFontSize` (14), `labelPadding` (5), `showTitle`
(true), `titleFontSize` (16), `titlePadding` (5), `showTick` (true), `tickLength` (5),
`tickWidth` (2), `showAxisLine` (true), `axisLineWidth` (2), `labelRotation` (0, **bottom
X axis only**).

## Theme Variables (`:148-199`)

Under `themeVariables.xyChart` — note the **capital C**, unlike the config key `xychart`
in the header keyword and `xyChart` in `config`. Easy to mistype.

`backgroundColor`, `titleColor`, `dataLabelColor`, `legendTextColor`, `xAxisLabelColor`,
`xAxisTitleColor`, `xAxisTickColor`, `xAxisLineColor`, `yAxisLabelColor`,
`yAxisTitleColor`, `yAxisTickColor`, `yAxisLineColor`, `plotColorPalette`.

`plotColorPalette` is a comma-separated string, applied **sequentially to plots in source
order** (`:179`). This is the hook for matching the app palette — wire it into
`packages/ui/src/theme.ts`.

## Editor Notes

- Completion at line start: `title`, `x-axis`, `y-axis`, `line`, `bar`; `horizontal` only
  immediately after `xychart`.
- Diagnostic: a series whose value count differs from the x-axis category count — the
  characteristic bug, and it renders without complaint.
- Diagnostic: a per-point label on a `bar` (silently ignored).
- Diagnostic: an unquoted multi-word value.
- Hint: an unnamed plot will not appear in the legend.
- Line-oriented; `StreamLanguage` is enough.

# Architecture Diagram

**Source**: `mermaid-upstream/packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/architecture.md` (332 lines)
**Detector**: `src/diagrams/architecture/architectureDetector.ts` — `/^\s*architecture/`
**Minimum version**: v11.1.0
**Registry id**: `architecture`

Building blocks: **groups, services, edges, junctions** (`:23`).

Conventions: **icons in `()`, labels in `[]`** (`:25`). Declaration order is free, but an
identifier must be declared before it is referenced (`:27`).

## Groups (`:29-49`)

```
group {id}({icon})[{title}] (in {parentId})?
group public_api(cloud)[Public API]
group private_api(cloud)[Private API] in public_api
```

## Services (`:51-71`)

```
service {id}({icon})[{title}] (in {parentId})?
service database1(database)[My Database] in private_api
```

## Junctions (`:218-244`)

```
junction {id} (in {parentId})?
```

A 4-way split point between edges.

## Edges (`:73-126`)

```
{serviceId}{{group}}?:{T|B|L|R} {<}?--{>}? {T|B|L|R}:{serviceId}{{group}}?
```

- The side each edge leaves from is given by `:T`, `:B`, `:L`, `:R`.
- Arrowheads: `<` before the left direction, `>` after the right direction —
  `subnet:R --> L:gateway`.
- Mixing sides produces a 90° edge: `db:T -- L:server`.
- **`{group}` modifier**: `server{group}:B --> T:subnet{group}` routes the edge out of the
  containing group rather than the service.
- **Group ids cannot be used in edges**, and `{group}` only works for services that are
  inside a group (`:126`). Both are diagnostics.

## Alignment (v11.16.0+) (`:128-216`)

```
align row {idA} {idB} {idC} ...
align column {idA} {idB} ...
```

Forces members onto a shared y (row) or x (column) so the layout heuristic cannot collapse
them onto the same coordinate.

- Members must already be declared as services or junctions; **at least two required**.
- One directive per line.
- Member order determines order along the axis.
- Choose the axis by port pair: `align column` when members share a horizontal port pair
  (`R --> L:x`), `align row` when they share a vertical one (`B --> T:x`).
- Gap is controlled by `idealEdgeLengthMultiplier`.

> **Order must not contradict edge directions** (`:175`). Given `a:L --> R:b` (which puts
> `a` right of `b`), `align row a b` makes the layout engine **fail to render**. This is a
> hard failure from a plausible-looking line, and a strong diagnostic candidate: the
> editor can detect the contradiction statically.

Grid layouts pair each `align row` with `align column` directives; columns may span rows
and cross groups (`:177-214`).

## Configuration

`randomize` (v11.14.0+, `:248-281`): boolean, default `false`.

> **Determinism warning** (`:252`): *"`randomize: false` alone is not enough to guarantee
> identical renders — the underlying fcose layout still calls `Math.random()`."* Use
> `seed`. **Our visual regression tests for architecture must pin `seed`**, same issue as
> cynefin.

Layout tuning (v11.15.0+, `:283-293`), passed through to fcose:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeSeparation` | `75` | Min px between siblings in a group |
| `idealEdgeLengthMultiplier` | `1.5` | Multiplier on `iconSize` for same-group edge length |
| `edgeElasticity` | `0.45` | Spring elasticity 0–1 on same-group edges |
| `numIter` | `2500` | Max fcose iterations |
| `seed` | `1` | Deterministic seed; `0` opts out to native `Math.random` |

Cross-group edges are unaffected by `idealEdgeLengthMultiplier` and `edgeElasticity`.

> These knobs tune force-direction only; they cannot separate siblings that share a
> logical position ([#6120](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/6120)) — that is
> what `align` is for (`:311`).

## Icons (`:313-332`)

Built in: `cloud`, `database`, `disk`, `internet`, `server`.

Anything else requires a registered icon pack, then `pack:icon-name` — e.g.
`logos:aws-lambda`. 200,000+ icons available via iconify.design.

> **Product decision needed.** Architecture diagrams are far less useful with five icons.
> Registering an iconify pack means either bundling it or fetching it at runtime — and
> phase 1 asserts zero outbound requests. Bundling a curated subset (`logos:`) inside the
> render frame is the option that keeps that promise. Track it as a feature spec.

## Editor Notes

- Completion for icon names is the highest-value feature here, and it depends on the icon
  pack decision above.
- Completion after `in` should offer declared group ids only.
- Completion after `:` should offer `T`, `B`, `L`, `R`.
- Diagnostics: reference to an undeclared id; a group id used in an edge; `{group}` on a
  service that is not in a group; `align` with fewer than two members; `align` order
  contradicting an edge direction.
- Fold by group.

1	# TreeView Diagram (v11.14.0+)
2	
3	## Introduction
4	
5	A TreeView diagram is used to represent hierarchical data in the form of a directory-like structure, with file/folder icons, connector lines, and optional annotations.
6	
7	## Syntax
8	
9	The structure of the tree depends only on indentation. Labels can be **bare** (unquoted) or **quoted** (for names containing spaces).
10	
11	- Directories are indicated by a trailing `/` on the label — they render in bold text.
12	- Icons are hidden by default — enable the built-in file/folder icons with the `showIcons` config option, or set one per node with `icon()`.
13	- Quoted labels (`"my file"`) support spaces in names.
14	
15	```
16	treeView-beta
17	    my-project/
18	        src/
19	            index.js
20	        package.json
21	        README.md
22	```
23	
24	Quoted labels (backward compatible):
25	
26	```
27	treeView-beta
28	    "my project"
29	        "folder with spaces"
30	            "file.js"
31	```
32	
33	## Box-Drawing Input
34	
35	As an alternative to indentation, you can use box-drawing characters to define the tree structure. The parser auto-detects the format — no extra keyword or config is needed. This is how most file tree diagrams are drawn already, so you can turn those into Mermaid diagrams with very little effort.
36	
37	Both standard (`├──`, `└──`, `│`) and heavy (`┣━━`, `┗━━`, `┃`) Unicode variants are supported.
38	
39	```mermaid-example
40	treeView-beta
41	├── src/
42	│   ├── index.ts
43	│   └── utils.ts
44	├── package.json
45	└── README.md
46	```
47	
48	All annotations work the same way — just append them after the label:
49	
50	```mermaid-example
51	treeView-beta
52	├── src/
53	│   ├── App.tsx :::highlight icon(logos:react) ## main component
54	│   └── index.ts ## entry point
55	├── .env ## environment variables
56	├── Dockerfile
57	└── package.json
58	```
59	
60	Depth is inferred from the column position of the branch character, so deeper nesting works naturally:
61	
62	```mermaid-example
63	treeView-beta
64	├── packages/
65	│   ├── mermaid/
66	│   │   ├── src/
67	│   │   │   ├── parser.ts
68	│   │   │   └── renderer.ts
69	│   │   └── package.json
70	│   └── parser/
71	│       └── src/
72	└── README.md
73	```
74	
75	> **Note:** If a parse error occurs, line numbers in the error message refer to your original input. Tab characters are automatically expanded to spaces.
76	
77	## Annotations
78	
79	### Highlighting with :::class
80	
81	Annotate a node with `:::className` to apply a CSS class. A built-in `highlight` class is provided:
82	
83	```mermaid-example
84	treeView-beta
85	    src/
86	        App.tsx :::highlight
87	        index.js
88	    package.json
89	```
90	
91	### Inline descriptions with `##`
92	
93	Add a visible description after `##` — rendered next to the label in italic:
94	
95	```mermaid-example
96	treeView-beta
97	    src/
98	        index.js ## app entry point
99	        config.ts ## runtime configuration
100	    package.json ## project manifest
101	```
102	
103	### Icons
104	
105	Icons are hidden by default. Set the `showIcons` config option to `true` to show the built-in icons — `file` for files and `folder` for directories:
106	
107	```mermaid-example
108	---
109	config:
110	  treeView:
111	    showIcons: true
112	---
113	treeView-beta
114	    src/
115	        index.js
116	    package.json
117	```
118	
119	#### File-type icons via config maps
120	
121	Mermaid ships no filename/extension mapping — file-type icons are fully user-configured through the `filenameIcons` and `extensionIcons` config options, using icons from a registered [icon pack](../config/icons.md) such as [material-icon-theme](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/material-icon-theme/). Values are resolved like `icon()` references — `pack:name` is used as-is, unprefixed names resolve via `defaultIconPack`, and `none` hides the icon for matching files. Directories and unmapped files keep the built-in `folder`/`file` icons:
122	
123	```mermaid-example
124	---
125	config:
126	  treeView:
127	    showIcons: true
128	    defaultIconPack: material-icon-theme
129	    filenameIcons:
130	      Dockerfile: docker
131	    extensionIcons:
132	      .ts: typescript
133	      .tsx: react-ts
134	      .txt: none
135	---
136	treeView-beta
137	    src/
138	        App.tsx
139	        utils.ts
140	    Dockerfile
141	    notes.txt
142	    README.md
143	```
144	
145	#### Icon overrides with icon()
146	
147	Set a node's icon explicitly with `icon(name)`, where `name` is any icon from a registered [icon pack](../config/icons.md), referenced as `pack:name`. Explicit icons always render, even when `showIcons` is off:
148	
149	```mermaid-example
150	treeView-beta
151	    src/
152	        App.tsx icon(logos:react)
153	        index.js
154	    package.json
155	```
156	
157	When `defaultIconPack` is set, unprefixed names resolve in that pack — `icon(rust)` becomes shorthand for `icon(material-icon-theme:rust)`. The built-in `file` and `folder` icons can always be referenced without a prefix, e.g. `icon(folder)`.
158	
159	```note
160	Icon packs are not bundled with Mermaid — they must be registered with `registerIconPacks` by the site embedding the diagram. See [registering icon packs](../config/icons.md). An unregistered icon renders as a question mark.
161	```
162	
163	#### Hiding icons
164	
165	When `showIcons` is enabled, use `icon()` or `icon(none)` to hide the icon of a single node:
166	
167	```mermaid-example
168	---
169	config:
170	  treeView:
171	    showIcons: true
172	---
173	treeView-beta
174	    src/
175	        index.js icon(none)
176	    package.json
177	```
178	
179	### Combined annotations
180	
181	Annotations can be combined in any order:
182	
183	```mermaid-example
184	treeView-beta
185	    my-project/
186	        src/
187	            App.tsx :::highlight icon(logos:react) ## main component
188	            index.js ## entry point
189	        .env ## environment variables
190	        Dockerfile
191	        package.json
192	```
193	
194	## Comments
195	
196	Use `%%` for invisible comments (standard Mermaid convention):
197	
198	```
199	treeView-beta
200	    %% Generated files — do not edit
201	    src/
202	        generated/
203	        index.js
204	```
205	
206	## Examples
207	
208	Basic with quoted labels:
209	
210	```mermaid-example
211	treeView-beta
212	    "packages"
213	        "mermaid"
214	            "src"
215	        "parser"
216	```
217	
218	Unicode and emoji in labels:
219	
220	Labels are rendered exactly as written — unicode characters and consecutive spaces are preserved. Since the built-in icons are hidden by default, emoji make handy inline icons:
221	
222	```mermaid-example
223	treeView-beta
224	    🚀 rocket-app/
225	        📦 packages/
226	            🎨 ui/
227	            🛠️ utils/
228	        🧪 tests/
229	        📝 README.md
230	        ⚙️ config.yaml
231	```
232	
233	With custom config:
234	
235	```mermaid-example
236	---
237	config:
238	    treeView:
239	        rowIndent: 80
240	        lineThickness: 3
241	    themeVariables:
242	        treeView:
243	            labelFontSize: '20px'
244	            labelColor: '#FF0000'
245	            lineColor: '#00FF00'
246	---
247	treeView-beta
248	    "packages"
249	        "mermaid"
250	            "src"
251	        "parser"
252	```
253	
254	## Config Variables
255	
256	| Property        | Description                                                                      | Default Value |
257	| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
258	| rowIndent       | Indentation for each row                                                         | 10            |
259	| paddingX        | Horizontal padding of row                                                        | 5             |
260	| paddingY        | Vertical padding of row                                                          | 5             |
261	| lineThickness   | Thickness of the line                                                            | 1             |
262	| showIcons       | Whether to show the default file/folder icons (explicit `icon()` always renders) | false         |
263	| defaultIconPack | Registered iconify pack used to resolve unprefixed icon references               | ''            |
264	| filenameIcons   | Filename → icon map for file-type icons                                          | {}            |
265	| extensionIcons  | Extension → icon map for file-type icons                                         | {}            |
266	
267	### Theme Variables
268	
269	| Property         | Description                                               | Default Value        |
270	| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
271	| labelFontSize    | Font size of the label                                    | '16px'               |
272	| labelColor       | Color of the label                                        | 'black'              |
273	| lineColor        | Color of the line                                         | 'black'              |
274	| iconColor        | Color of icons (applies to icons that use `currentColor`) | '#546e7a'            |
275	| descriptionColor | Color of `##` description text                            | '#6a9955'            |
276	| highlightBg      | Highlight background fill                                 | rgba(255,193,7,0.15) |
277	| highlightStroke  | Highlight border stroke                                   | #ffc107              |
278

1	# Event Modeling Diagram (v11.15.0+)
2	
3	## Introduction
4	
5	> **Event Modeling** (EM) is a method of describing systems using an example of how information has changed within them over time. Event Modeling specifically omits transient details and looks at what the information flow is and what the user sees at any particular point in time.
6	
7	You can read more at [Event Modeling web page](https://eventmodeling.org/).
8	
9	Event Modeling diagram is composed of a few main entities:
10	
11	- Trigger - UI and Processor
12	- Command
13	- View / Read Model
14	- Event
15	
16	Entities are organized in swimlanes forming a timeline usually based on the following patterns:
17	
18	- State View
19	- State Change
20	- Translation
21	- Automation
22	
23	You can find more details in the [cheat sheet](https://eventmodeling.org/posts/event-modeling-cheatsheet/).
24	
25	The purpose of the Domain Specific Language (DSL) supporting the drawing of the Event Modeling diagram is the rapid creation. Relations among the entities are inferred by default, so the distraction while you design is limited. Further detail to the entities can be added gradually.
26	
27	The grammar for the DSL is also maintained in a [separate project](https://github.com/lgazo/event-modeling-dsl) with the intention to provide also different types of output, VS Code (and potentially other) IDEs, etc.
28	
29	## Basic Syntax
30	
31	The DSL supports two types of syntaxes - compact and relaxed one. Both will be mentioned in the examples and both can be used interchangeably.
32	
33	### Timeline
34	
35	The timeline is the key part of the diagram and it is composed of **Time Frame** definitions. Speedy Time Frame typing is the key of the compact notation. For compact notation you type the `tf` token. For the relaxed notation you type `timeframe` token.
36	
37	```md
38	eventmodeling
39	
40	tf 01 ui CartUI
41	tf 02 cmd AddItem
42	tf 03 evt ItemAdded
43	```
44	
45	rendering to
46	
47	```mermaid
48	eventmodeling
49	
50	tf 01 ui CartUI
51	tf 02 cmd AddItem
52	tf 03 evt ItemAdded
53	```
54	
55	Each Time Frame is referenced by a **unique number** in order to distinguish one from another and also to be able to reference it when needed. Depending on the complexity of the diagram it should be enough to have just two digit number or more. Imagine you are typing a BASIC program on your ZX Spectrum always starting with a two digit number, but the order of the numbers does not matter, just the uniqueness in the whole timeline.
56	
57	The Time Frame also contains an **Entity Identifier**, e.g. in case of `01` Time Frame it is `CartUI`. One Entity Identifier can be used multiple times in the timeline for example when you want to express invocations of the same event in different points in time.
58	
59	Relaxed notation would look like this:
60	
61	```md
62	eventmodeling
63	
64	timeframe 01 ui CartUI
65	timeframe 02 command AddItem
66	timeframe 03 event ItemAdded
67	```
68	
69	### Inline data
70	
71	It is possible to provide data examples for individual Time Frames. An Inline Data is wrapped in curly brackets on the same line as the Time Frame.
72	
73	Compact version:
74	
75	```mermaid-example
76	eventmodeling
77	
78	tf 01 ui CartUI
79	tf 02 cmd AddItem { description: string }
80	tf 03 evt ItemAdded { description: string }
81	```
82	
83	Relaxed version:
84	
85	```mermaid-example
86	eventmodeling
87	
88	timeframe 01 ui CartUI
89	timeframe 02 command AddItem { description: string }
90	timeframe 03 event ItemAdded { description: string }
91	```
92	
93	### Data block
94	
95	If you need to provide more complex data description, you can define the **Data Block** separately. Data Block is referenced from a Time Frame by providing the identifier inside of double-square brackets `[[identifier]]`, similar to wiki links convention in Markdown.
96	
97	In case the same entity is repeated you need to uniquely identify the data blocks, therefore the Data Block identifier is suffixed with a number.
98	
99	Compact version:
100	
101	```mermaid-example
102	eventmodeling
103	
104	tf 01 ui CartUI
105	tf 02 cmd AddItem [[AddItem01]]
106	tf 03 evt ItemAdded [[ItemAdded]]
107	tf 04 cmd AddItem [[AddItem02]]
108	tf 05 evt ItemAdded [[ItemAdded]]
109	
110	data AddItem01 {
111	  description: 'john'
112	  image: 'avatar_john'
113	  price: 20.4
114	}
115	
116	data AddItem02 {
117	  description: 'jack'
118	  image: 'avatar_jack'
119	  price: 12.5
120	}
121	
122	data ItemAdded {
123	  description: string
124	  image: string
125	  price: number
126	}
127	```
128	
129	Relaxed version:
130	
131	```mermaid-example
132	eventmodeling
133	
134	timeframe 01 ui CartUI
135	timeframe 02 command AddItem [[AddItem01]]
136	timeframe 03 event ItemAdded [[ItemAdded]]
137	timeframe 04 command AddItem [[AddItem02]]
138	timeframe 05 event ItemAdded [[ItemAdded]]
139	
140	data AddItem01 {
141	  description: 'john'
142	  image: 'avatar_john'
143	  price: 20.4
144	}
145	
146	data AddItem02 {
147	  description: 'jack'
148	  image: 'avatar_jack'
149	  price: 12.5
150	}
151	
152	data ItemAdded {
153	  description: string
154	  image: string
155	  price: number
156	}
157	```
158	
159	### Resetting the flow
160	
161	By default the diagram builds the relations based on the inference. But modeling a more complex business flow requires to break such inference from time to time. For that you can use a different type of Time Frame called **Reset Frame**. It is represented by a `rf` / `resetframe` token.
162	
163	Compact version:
164	
165	```mermaid-example
166	eventmodeling
167	
168	tf 01 ui CartUI
169	tf 02 cmd AddItem
170	tf 03 evt ItemAdded
171	
172	rf 04 evt External.InventoryChanged
173	tf 05 pcr InventoryProcessor
174	tf 06 cmd ChangeInventory
175	tf 07 evt Cart.InventoryChanged
176	```
177	
178	Relaxed version:
179	
180	```mermaid-example
181	eventmodeling
182	
183	timeframe 01 ui CartUI
184	timeframe 02 command AddItem
185	timeframe 03 event ItemAdded
186	
187	resetframe 04 event External.InventoryChanged
188	timeframe 05 processor InventoryProcessor
189	timeframe 06 command ChangeInventory
190	timeframe 07 event Cart.InventoryChanged
191	```
192	
193	### Multiple relations
194	
195	There are situations where you need to specify multiple relations for an entity. For example when a **Read Model** is built of multiple **Events**. You can use `->>` token for that.
196	
197	```mermaid-example
198	eventmodeling
199	
200	rf 02 evt CartCreated
201	rf 03 evt ItemAdded
202	rf 04 evt ItemRemoved
203	rf 05 evt CartCleared
204	tf 01 rmo CartUI ->> 02 ->> 03 ->> 04 ->> 05
205	```
206	
207	## Event Modeling patterns
208	
209	This chapter briefly summarizes each Event Modeling pattern.
210	
211	### State Change
212	
213	```mermaid-example
214	eventmodeling
215	
216	tf 01 ui CartUI
217	tf 02 cmd AddItem
218	tf 03 evt ItemAdded
219	```
220	
221	### State View
222	
223	```mermaid-example
224	eventmodeling
225	
226	tf 03 evt ItemAdded
227	tf 02 rmo CartItems
228	tf 04 ui CartUI
229	```
230	
231	### Translation
232	
233	```mermaid-example
234	eventmodeling
235	
236	tf 03 evt External.InventoryChanged
237	tf 02 pcr InventoryProcessor
238	tf 04 cmd ChangeInventory
239	tf 05 evt Cart.InventoryChanged
240	```
241	
242	## Details of the Syntax
243	
244	### Entity types
245	
246	Entity type is determined by the third column in the Time Frame grammar.
247	
248	Compact version:
249	
250	```md
251	tf 01 pcr InventoryProcessor
252	```
253	
254	Relaxed version:
255	
256	```md
257	timeframe 01 processor InventoryProcessor
258	```
259	
260	Entities are assigned to default swimlanes unless a **Namespace** is specified in the Entity Identifier.
261	
262	There are the following types available:
263	
264	- `ui`: UI - belongs to UI/Automation swimlane
265	- `pcr` / `processor`: Processor - belongs to UI/Automation swimlane
266	- `cmd` / `command`: Command - belongs to Command/Read Model swimlane
267	- `rmo` / `readmodel`: Read Model - belongs to Command/Read Model swimlane
268	- `evt` / `event`: Event - belongs to Events swimlane
269	
270	### Swimlanes and Namespaces
271	
272	There are three basic **Swimlanes** inferred from the Entity Type.
273	
274	- UI/Automation
275	- Command/Read Model
276	- Events
277	
278	As your diagram grows and you explore the depths of a particular software system, you want to categorize your Entities as well. In order to do that, you can use **Namespace** identifier as part of the Entity Identifier.
279	
280	```md
281	Inventory.InventoryChanged
282	```
283	
284	**Namespace** is the first part before the `.` of the Entity Identifier. Each combination of the Namespace and Entity type forms new Swimlane. The order how they are specified in the text definition specifies the order of the Swimlanes in the diagram.
285	
286	```mermaid-example
287	eventmodeling
288	
289	rf 01 evt Inventory.InventoryChanged
290	rf 02 evt External.InventoryChanged
291	```
292	
293	### Data block data types
294	
295	A **Data** is always wrapped in curly brackets. It can be prepended by a data type in backticks. The pattern applies for **Inline Data** as well as for **Data Block**.
296	
297	```md
298	tf 01 rmo UserAdded `json`{ "name": "foo" }
299	```
300	
301	or for Data Block
302	
303	```md
304	data UserAdded01 `json`{
305	"name": "foo"
306	}
307	```
308	
309	```warning
310	There is no special treatment in the diagram renderer at the moment for a specific data type.
311	```
312	
313	Supported types are:
314	
315	- `json`
316	- `jsobj`
317	- `figma`
318	- `salt`
319	- `uri`
320	- `md`
321	- `html`
322	- `text`
323

# TreeView

**Source**: `mermaid-upstream/packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/treeView.md` (277 lines)
**Detector**: `src/diagrams/treeView/detector.ts` — `/^\s*treeView-beta/`
**Minimum version**: v11.14.0
**Registry id**: `treeview`

Note the **camelCase keyword**: `treeView-beta`. The detector is case-sensitive.

## Two Input Formats

### Indentation (`:7-31`)

```
treeView-beta
    my-project/
        src/
            index.js
        package.json
```

- A **trailing `/` marks a directory** and renders it bold.
- Labels may be bare or quoted; quotes allow spaces.

### Box-drawing characters (`:33-75`)

The parser **auto-detects** this format — no keyword, no config:

```
treeView-beta
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts
│   └── utils.ts
└── README.md
```

Both standard (`├──`, `└──`, `│`) and heavy (`┣━━`, `┗━━`, `┃`) variants work. Depth comes
from the column position of the branch character.

> This is the single best feature in the type: `tree` output and README file listings
> paste in and render. The editor should make that discoverable — a paste of text starting
> with `├──` is a strong signal to offer conversion to a treeView diagram.

Tabs are expanded to spaces automatically, and parse-error line numbers refer to the
original input (`:75`).

## Annotations (`:77-192`)

Appended after the label, **combinable in any order**:

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `:::className` | CSS class; `highlight` is built in |
| `## text` | inline description, rendered italic beside the label |
| `icon(name)` | explicit icon; renders even when `showIcons` is off |
| `icon()` / `icon(none)` | hide this node's icon |

Example: `App.tsx :::highlight icon(logos:react) ## main component`

## Icons (`:103-177`)

- Hidden by default. `showIcons: true` enables the built-in `file` and `folder` icons.
- **Mermaid ships no filename or extension mapping** (`:121`). File-type icons are entirely
  user-configured via `filenameIcons` and `extensionIcons`.
- Resolution: `pack:name` is used as-is; an unprefixed name resolves via `defaultIconPack`;
  `none` hides it. `file` and `folder` always resolve without a prefix.
- **Icon packs are not bundled with mermaid** (`:159-161`). An unregistered icon renders as
  a question mark.

> Same product decision as the architecture diagram: registering an iconify pack conflicts
> with the phase-1 promise of zero outbound requests unless a curated subset is bundled
> inside the render frame. Track both together in one feature spec.

## Comments (`:194-204`)

`%%`, standard.

## Unicode And Emoji (`:218-231`)

Labels render **exactly as written**; unicode and consecutive spaces are preserved. Since
icons are off by default, emoji are the practical inline icon. Worth surfacing in the
starter snippet.

## Config Variables (`:254-265`)

| Property | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `rowIndent` | `10` |
| `paddingX` | `5` |
| `paddingY` | `5` |
| `lineThickness` | `1` |
| `showIcons` | `false` |
| `defaultIconPack` | `''` |
| `filenameIcons` | `{}` |
| `extensionIcons` | `{}` |

## Theme Variables (`:267-277`)

`labelFontSize` (`'16px'`), `labelColor` (`black`), `lineColor` (`black`), `iconColor`
(`#546e7a`, applies to icons using `currentColor`), `descriptionColor` (`#6a9955`),
`highlightBg` (`rgba(255,193,7,0.15)`), `highlightStroke` (`#ffc107`).

The defaults are hardcoded light-theme colors — `black` labels and lines. **This type will
be unreadable in dark mode** unless we override `labelColor` and `lineColor` from the
token set. Add it to `packages/ui/src/theme.ts`.

## Editor Notes

- Two tokenizers, selected by auto-detection on the first content line: indentation-based
  and box-drawing-based. Mixing them within one document is undefined — check the grammar
  before allowing it.
- Completion: `:::highlight` and `icon(` after a label; class names from `classDef` if
  supported; extension keys from `extensionIcons` in the config.
- Diagnostic: an `icon(pack:name)` whose pack is not registered, since it silently becomes
  a question mark.
- Fold by directory.

# Event Modeling

**Source**: `mermaid-upstream/packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/eventmodeling.md` (322 lines)
**Detector**: `src/diagrams/eventmodeling/detector.ts` — `/^\s*eventmodeling/`
**Minimum version**: v11.15.0
**Registry id**: `eventmodeling`

Grammar is also maintained in a separate project,
[event-modeling-dsl](https://github.com/lgazo/event-modeling-dsl) (`:27`) — a second
source to consult when the page is ambiguous.

## Two Interchangeable Notations

Every keyword has a **compact** and a **relaxed** form, freely mixable in one document
(`:31`):

| Compact | Relaxed |
| --- | --- |
| `tf` | `timeframe` |
| `rf` | `resetframe` |
| `ui` | `ui` |
| `pcr` | `processor` |
| `cmd` | `command` |
| `rmo` | `readmodel` |
| `evt` | `event` |

## Time Frames (`:33-58`)

```
tf <number> <entityType> <EntityIdentifier> [data]
tf 01 ui CartUI
```

- The number must be **unique across the timeline**; **order does not matter** (`:55`).
  Upstream's analogy is BASIC line numbers.
- One entity identifier may appear at several time frames, to express repeated invocations.

## Entity Types And Swimlanes (`:244-291`)

| Type | Swimlane |
| --- | --- |
| `ui` | UI/Automation |
| `pcr` / `processor` | UI/Automation |
| `cmd` / `command` | Command/Read Model |
| `rmo` / `readmodel` | Command/Read Model |
| `evt` / `event` | Events |

**Namespaces**: the part of the entity identifier before the first `.` —
`Inventory.InventoryChanged`. **Each namespace + entity-type combination forms a new
swimlane**, and declaration order determines swimlane order in the diagram (`:284`).

That last rule is unusual and worth surfacing: reordering two lines can restructure the
whole diagram.

## Reset Frames (`:159-191`)

Relations are inferred by default. `rf` / `resetframe` breaks the inference chain, which
is what makes more complex business flows expressible.

## Multiple Relations (`:193-205`)

`->>` chains a frame to several others — typically a read model built from many events:

```
tf 01 rmo CartUI ->> 02 ->> 03 ->> 04 ->> 05
```

Note the targets are **time-frame numbers**, not entity identifiers.

## Data (`:69-157`, `:293-323`)

**Inline**, on the same line, in curly brackets:

```
tf 02 cmd AddItem { description: string }
```

**Data block**, referenced with wiki-style double square brackets:

```
tf 02 cmd AddItem [[AddItem01]]

data AddItem01 {
  description: 'john'
  price: 20.4
}
```

When the same entity repeats, data block identifiers are suffixed with a number to keep
them unique (`:97`).

**Data types** are prepended in backticks, for both inline and block forms:

```
tf 01 rmo UserAdded `json`{ "name": "foo" }
data UserAdded01 `json`{ "name": "foo" }
```

Supported: `json`, `jsobj`, `figma`, `salt`, `uri`, `md`, `html`, `text`.

> **No renderer treatment yet** (`:309-311`) — the type is parsed and ignored. Offer it in
> completion, but say in the detail text that it currently has no visual effect.

## Patterns (`:207-240`)

The page documents four canonical shapes, which make excellent starter snippets:

- **State Change**: `ui` → `cmd` → `evt`
- **State View**: `evt` → `rmo` → `ui`
- **Translation**: `evt` → `pcr` → `cmd` → `evt`
- **Automation** (named at `:21`, not exemplified)

## Editor Notes

- Completion should offer the **compact** forms first — the whole design goal of the DSL
  is rapid typing (`:25`, `:35`) — with the relaxed form as the detail text.
- Completion after `->>` should offer time-frame numbers declared in the document.
- Diagnostics: a duplicate time-frame number; a `->>` referencing an undeclared number; a
  `[[identifier]]` with no matching `data` block; an unknown data type in backticks.
- Fold `data … { }` blocks.
- Offer the four patterns as snippets, not just one starter.
